abstract: Let $f$ be a positive integer, and let $χ$ be a primitive quadratic character of conductor $f$. Let $k$ be a positive integer, and write $B_k(χ,X)$ for the $k$-th Bernoulli polynomial corresponding to $χ$. Suppose $B_k(χ,X)$ is irreducible and of degree at least $2$. Then for 100% of positive integers $m$ divisible by $f$, the Diophantine equation \[ χ(1) \cdot (x+1)^k+χ(2) \cdot (x+2)^k+\cdots+χ(m) \cdot (x+m)^k \, =\, y^n, \] has no solutions with $x$, $y$, $n$ integers, and $n \ge 2$.
title: On a character-twisted analogue of Schäffer's equation
